name: Abyss Nexus Network
trait: Warp from anywhere — mid-ride, mid-fall, mid-swim
summary: Two kinds of fast-travel point cover Pywel. Step on an Abyss Nexus to add it to the map; at an Abyss Cresset, solve the puzzle it sets. Patches made the network the game's biggest time-saver: more Nexuses in 1.00.03, faster loading in 1.01, warping while moving in 1.02, and since 1.03 from horseback, mid-fall, swimming or climbing.

impact.basis: One map click replaces any ride; since 1.03 it works mounted, falling, swimming and climbing (patch notes).

reach.basis: Every region, every session: points sit in cities, settlements, the Greymane Camp and the countryside.

unlock.basis: Step on a Nexus to add it. Cressets add a puzzle. Nothing to buy.

steps: Step onto any Abyss Nexus to add it to the map.
At an Abyss Cresset, take the Abyss Artifact it offers and solve the puzzle that starts.
Check the map's large question marks: these Mysterious Energy areas usually hold a Nexus and a Cresset.
Open the map on the All or Environment tab and select a point. Points do not show on the Quest or Faction tabs.

location: Cities, major settlements, the Greymane Camp and the open country; Mysterious Energy areas on the map.
notes: Carrying an apprehended outlaw blocks fast travel, and warping away fails the bounty. Drop the outlaw first.

name: Royler
trait: The fastest horse in Pywel, waiting just north of Hernand
summary: The travel upgrade you can have in the first hours. Royler stands by a lake in the Silverwolf Mountains, a short ride north of the City of Hernand, and tops every horse on Speed and Acceleration with the deepest stamina of any mount on record. The ride from the last Nexus to the target shrinks.

impact.basis: Top Speed and Acceleration with 390 Stamina at Lv 5 and a second boost out of every drift (Mounts plate).

reach.basis: Every land journey between Nexuses, all game long.

unlock.basis: A taming minigame at a lake near the starting city; Stamina Lv 6 needed.

remedy.fixes: Long rides on a starter horse between fast-travel points.
remedy.gain: Top speed on the longest stamina bar, from the first hours of the game.

name: Blackstar
trait: Fly anywhere in a straight line
summary: Kliff's dragon, earned at the close of Chapter 11. It flies over mountains and water to anywhere on the continent, which no road or Nexus does. Each summon lasts about fifteen real minutes, then needs about fifty to recover.

impact.basis: True flight in a straight line over any terrain (Mounts plate).

reach.basis: All of Pywel, but about 15 real minutes per summon and about 50 of cooldown.

unlock.basis: Main story through Chapter 11.

remedy.fixes: Terrain between you and the target.
remedy.gain: A straight line over mountains and water.
watch: Resting does not shorten the cooldown, and it cannot be summoned inside the Abyss.

name: Flight
trait: Crow wings: glide off any height
summary: White Crow's crow wings let Kliff glide from any height until his stamina runs out. Swift Flight, the level-2 upgrade, trades more stamina for more speed. Patches lowered the stamina cost of flying and gliding, and 1.03 made the Focused Aerial Roll an official skill: a forward burst paid in Spirit instead of Stamina.

impact.basis: Turns every cliff and tower into a launch point; Swift Flight adds speed.

reach.basis: Anywhere you can jump from height, every session.

unlock.basis: Two main quests, Abyss Without Balance then Woman in White; one Abyss Artifact for Swift Flight.

requires: Main quest Abyss Without Balance, then Woman in White (Hernand)

steps: Finish Abyss Without Balance, then play Woman in White in Hernand.
Speak to White Crow the Witch when it ends: she gives Kliff the crow wings, and Flight unlocks on the red skill tree.
Jump from height and press Square, X or C in mid-air to glide.
Spend one Abyss Artifact on Swift Flight for speed at a higher stamina cost.

location: Story unlock in Hernand — no world location.
notes: Flight cannot start from the ground.
Stamina levels and Movement Speed gear both stretch a glide.
since: Base game · cheaper and faster by patch

name: Axiom Force
trait: Grab, launch and swing: ranks 2 and 3 make it traversal
summary: Axiom Force grabs objects and enemies at range. Rank 2 adds Aerial Maneuver, which launches Kliff into the air after a grab; rank 3 adds Aerial Swing, which swings him the way he steers. Patch 1.03 gave Damiane and Oongka the skill too.

impact.basis: Launch and swing add routes up and across; puzzles need it anyway.

reach.basis: Traversal and puzzles all over Pywel.

unlock.basis: Unlocked in Chapter 1; ranks 2 and 3 cost Abyss Artifacts.

steps: Axiom Force unlocks during Chapter 1.
Spend Abyss Artifacts in the skill tree: rank 2 for Aerial Maneuver, rank 3 for Aerial Swing.
Hold L3 / LS (Tab on keyboard) to grab, then launch or swing.

location: Story unlock — no world location.

name: Thinker's Meadow Nexus
trait: A broken Nexus beside the camp, mended with a Kuku Pot
summary: A fast-travel point near Howling Hill that starts broken. Fixing it takes three Chapter 2–4 unlocks: Karin Quarry cleared for House Roberts, the Kuku Pot from Grimnir's kiln quest, and Focused Force Palm. Then you carry an Abyss Transporter from the quarry in the pot and punch it into place.

impact.basis: Saves the ride from the nearest working point; how much depends on which others you hold.

reach.basis: Every trip to the camp while it sits at Howling Hill.

unlock.basis: Estate in Dismay, the Kiln Repair quest and Focused Force Palm, then a puzzle.

requires: Estate in Dismay (House Roberts): Karin Quarry liberated, the relic lifted
Kiln Repair at the Kilnden Workshop (Chapter 4), for the Kuku Pot

steps: In Karin Quarry, drop through the hole beneath where the giant relic was and head west.
Destroy the turrets, then smash the bismuth wall on the left with Focused Force Palm.
Behind it, grab the Abyss Transporter pad with Axiom Force and seal it in the Kuku Pot.
At Thinker's Meadow, burn the vines off the Nexus with Blinding Flash.
Release the Transporter from the pot, move it over the gap with Axiom Force and Force Palm it down into place.
Stand on it to unlock fast travel.

location: Thinker's Meadow, near Howling Hill, Hernand.

name: Ocean Drifter
trait: The fastest way to travel underwater
summary: The top underwater mount. An ancient diving machine sealed about 55 metres down in the Forgotten Ocean Ruins, it outruns every sea creature and your ship below the surface. It only works submerged, and surfacing locks it out for an hour.

impact.basis: The fastest underwater mount, faster than your ship (Mounts plate).

reach.basis: One activity: underwater, from about 30 m down.

unlock.basis: Charting the Unknown, a diving suit, and a dive into the Forgotten Ocean Ruins.

remedy.fixes: Crossing the seabed at swimming speed on a breath timer.
remedy.gain: Outruns every sea creature, and your ship, below the surface.
watch: Surfacing, warping away or summoning another mount starts a 60-minute real-time cooldown.

name: Diving Suits
trait: Minutes more air per dive, bought with relics
summary: Diving gear raises maximum breathing, the clock on every dive. The pre-order Charter's Diving Set adds up to 240 seconds at its starting refinement. The Marine Charter's set, sold for Ancient Relics by Sulivan at the Silvermoon Tradehouse, gives about half that and adds 2% swim speed on its gloves and boots.

reach.basis: One activity: diving in Charting the Unknown's seas.

unlock.basis: Twenty-two Ancient Relics at one shop, or a pre-order claim.

Go to Sulivan's Relic Exchange at the Silvermoon Tradehouse, Demeniss Port. If nobody is there, finish the Demeniss faction quest Silvermoon Trade Group first.
Buy the helm, gloves and boots for 5 relics each and the suit for 7: 22 for the set.

routes.label: Charter's Diving Set (pre-order)
steps: Pause, open Others → Options → Add-ons, and claim the Pre-order Exclusive Bonus under Receivable Items: eight pieces across two sets.

notes: The Marine Charter's set starts at Refinement 0; refining raises its breathing.

impact.basis: +600 maximum breathing and a swim-speed boost (PlayNews).

reach.basis: One activity: diving in Charting the Unknown's seas.

unlock.basis: A 168 m dive in the Dead Coral Sea; the upgrade is another deep chest.

steps: Reach the north-west of the Dead Coral Sea, far east of Delesyia, by ship or flying mount.

Equip it; Kliff, Damiane and Oongka can all wear it.

trait: Plate that breathes: up to 615 seconds more air
summary: A four-piece plate set for Kliff and Oongka that adds maximum breathing on every piece and 4% swim speed on three. Each piece sits in a fixed underwater chest sealed in a green rock that Force Palm breaks. Fully refined it adds 615 seconds of air. Damiane's version is the Sunken Azuretide set.

impact.basis: Every piece adds breathing; the full set at Refinement 10 adds 615 s (GamingBolt).

reach.basis: One activity: diving in Charting the Unknown's seas.

unlock.basis: Four chests from 15 m to 215 m down, each behind Force Palm.

steps: Boots: about 15 m down off the north-west coast of Razanui Island, west of the Great Coral Reef.
Armor: about 60 m down in a sunken shipwreck by the islets north-east of Ocula Island; the chest is mid-wreck.
Gloves: about 125 m down by a large coral formation south of the 'R' of the Great Coral Reef label.
Helm: about 215 m down on the Great Hydrothermal Vents, north of the map label's 'T', beside a smaller spire north-west of the largest.
Break each green rock with Force Palm and open the chest.

location: Four chests across the South Sea: Razanui, the Great Coral Reef, the Great Hydrothermal Vents and Ocula Island.
notes: The Helm also grants Daze immunity and Spirit regeneration (KeenGamer).

name: Bags
trait: Small +1, Medium +3, Large +5 — permanent
summary: Kliff starts with 50 inventory slots, and every bag adds slots for good: a Small Bag one, a Medium three, a Large five, while campaign milestones hand out bags of up to ten. Small Bags cost 50 copper at almost any vendor. The 27 Greymane Commissions alone are worth 81 slots. Carried inventory stops at 240 slots; past the cap, expansion rewards turn into boxes of materials.

impact.basis: Every Medium Bag is three fewer trips to sell or store.

reach.basis: Every session: the bag fills wherever you go.

unlock.basis: Small Bags at any vendor for 50 copper; Medium and Large from quests.

Run the Greymane Commissions: 27 of them, +81 slots in all.

name: Pets
trait: Loots the fallen so you do not have to
summary: Raise a stray animal's Trust to 100 and it becomes a pet. A summoned pet loots fallen enemies for you, with no filter, so it takes everything. Since 1.11 the Pets challenges raise registration to 100, with up to 50 out at camp; one follows you at a time. Patches added birds, five new cats and the Abyss Heuklang.

reach.basis: Every fight, everywhere.

unlock.basis: Stray dogs and cats from the first town: pet and feed to 100 Trust.

Summon it from Inventory → Pets. If it goes missing, unsummon and summon it again.

location: Strays in towns and camps; birds at a placed bird feeder.
notes: Pets do not fight unless they wear a Sigil of Valor; see Pet Sigils.

name: Extraction
trait: Take an upgrade back and keep the rare materials
summary: Since 1.06 a Smithy rolls a weapon, armour piece or accessory back to a lower refinement and returns what the upgrade cost: Abyss Artifacts and Aeserion’s Scales in full, ore, hide and bone at about 70%. The item keeps its socketed Abyss Gear and cannot drop below the level it came at.

reach.basis: Every gear swap.

unlock.basis: Any Smithy; Hernand’s is open early.

name: Lost Gear Recovery
area: Shops · Carl at the Greymane Camp
trait: Sold or lost a rare piece? It comes back to the shops
summary: Since 1.11 shopkeepers collect rare equipment you lose, from quests, treasure chests and other one-off sources, and offer it back for sale within seven days, at more than it was worth. Rare Kuku Pot items you discard go to Carl at the camp, who sells them back from his Recover Items tab.

impact.basis: A one-of-a-kind weapon sold by mistake is no longer gone for good.

reach.basis: Only when something rare is lost.

unlock.basis: Built in; pay the buyback price.

name: Movement Speed Gear
trait: Faster on foot and in the air: +22% glide at 15 ranks
summary: Movement Speed on gear speeds running and gliding: 15 ranks make a glide about 22% faster. Vulkk's build reaches it with Tariv Cloth Boots (Tariv's tailor, at 100 Trust) or Rabbit Cloth Boots (Demeniss Wildlife Park tailor), a Movement Speed shield, Ancient Earrings and Swift III Abyss Gears. Blackwing Leather Armor, from Crowcaller in Chapter 5, adds a rank early.

impact.basis: About +22% glide speed at 15 ranks (The Games Wiki); running gains too.

reach.basis: Every step and glide, everywhere.

Blackwing Leather Armor: defeat Crowcaller in Chapter 5.
Socket Swift III Abyss Gears into free slots.
Swap into the speed set before a long glide and back to combat gear on landing.

remedy.fixes: Slow jogs and short glides between points.
remedy.gain: More ground per stride and per glide.

summary: The cold halves Stamina regeneration in Pailune and the frozen mountains. Ice Resistance Level 5 makes you immune to that, and higher levels resist freezing attacks. One Level 5 cloak is enough: the Frostcursed Plate Cloak sits in a chest at the Sanctum of Expiation, and Bear Hide and Wolf cloaks sell at provisioners. Kuku Ice-Resistant Armor, at Level 10, adds complete freeze immunity.

impact.basis: Removes a −50% Stamina regeneration penalty (Vulkk).

reach.basis: Cold regions only: Pailune, the Everfrost and the snowbound peaks.

Burn the thorny roots with Blinding Flash, crawl down the passage and turn right to the chest.

name: Resting
trait: Skip up to 12 hours: every timer finishes sooner
summary: Every timer in Pywel runs on the in-game clock, roughly one hour per two real minutes: dispatches, bank cycles, builds, bag respawns. Sleeping in a bed or tent, or waiting at a campfire, skips up to 12 hours at a time.

impact.basis: Turns a wait of hours into a few seconds.

reach.basis: Every timed system: dispatch, building, banking, respawns.

unlock.basis: Any bed, tent or campfire.

name: Auto-Repeat Dispatch
trait: Resource missions that renew themselves
summary: Since 1.04 the dispatch board has two buttons: send once, or repeat. Repeat missions renew on their own, so food, Camp Funds and material runs keep going without re-assigning the team. Missions that pay Abyss Artifacts or other rare items stay one-shot.

impact.basis: No re-assigning teams after every run.

reach.basis: Every resource mission you keep running.

unlock.basis: The camp dispatch board, from Chapter 3.

Pick a resource mission and assign the team.

name: Camp Expansion
trait: Each tier opens storage, vendors and dispatch slots
summary: Howling Hill grows through expansion missions you dispatch from the map. Each tier adds facilities, mission slots and recruits, and private storage grows with it. The first costs 2 recruits, 100 food and 250 silver and finishes in 18 in-game hours; the fourth takes 10 recruits and 100,000. Since 1.04 the camp level also unlocks bigger house layouts.

impact.basis: More storage, vendors, dispatch slots and recruits at every tier.

reach.basis: Every trip to camp and every dispatch.

unlock.basis: Chapter 3 onward; costs climb steeply by the fourth tier.

steps: Advance the Grounds of the Sunrise faction quests; Marius opens new recruitment after each tier.
Open the map, select Howling Hill and start the expansion from its Missions menu.
Let the timer run (18 in-game hours for the first) or rest to skip it.

summary: The last camp move. Storage reaches its 1,000-slot ceiling, the Spacious Pailune house layout opens, the farm and ranch grow, and since 1.03 the key NPCs and vendors stand closer together. The move is permanent.

summary: Camp Funds pay for ships, leases and camp projects, and since patch 2.01 every Silver donated to Carl buys 1,000 of them. That shrinks the DLC's big prices: the 6,000,000 Large Hernandian Ship is 6,000 Silver, twelve Gold Bars.

summary: The quickest way to stop counting coins. A Witch turns one Golden Apple and three Gold Ore into a Gold Bar, and a bank pays 500 Silver for it. The recipe sits in the Witch's Hideout south of Pailune.

reach.basis: Every dispatch you run.

trait: Businesses that earn, and make gear, while you explore
